narrative:
The model determined that you have a 75% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this predicted risk is quite high, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your class rank at the end of your third year was the strongest influence; being in the second decile is substantially lower than the average of roughly sixth-decile performance among students who were accepted. This low ranking strongly pushed the prediction toward failure. Your first-year class rank, also in the second decile compared with an average around the sixth decile for accepted students, added further weight in the same direction, though less strongly.

Your undergraduate GPA of 3.20 worked mildly in your favor. It sits only slightly below the 3.23 average of accepted students and therefore nudged the prediction a little toward passing. Unfortunately, this positive effect was not large enough to offset the impact of your class rankings.

You should focus on strengthening the areas the model weighed most heavily. Retaking key courses to improve your GPA, seeking academic support, or gaining additional legal experience before reapplying could help demonstrate a clearer trajectory of success. Consider consulting an admissions advisor to identify programs that place greater emphasis on other strengths you may possess.
